newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday thanks to the continuing bullish performance of the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 11.2 percent from 10.5 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market surged to 11.3 million lots from 5.3 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said solid gains on the A share markets triggered heavy institutional borrowing on the repurchase market.
"The A share markets performed strongly, which fanned demand on the repo market and pushed up the rates," said one trader.
Trader said an issue of 72 million shares by an A share company in Shenzhen at the high price of 7.76 yuan also attracted large funds from the repo market, helping push up the repo rates.
The rates are likely to undergo a technical correction on Tuesday after today's heavy gains, traders said.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Monday despite their high yields with the market being ignored by most investors due to the bull run on the A share markets, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 118.56 yuan from 118.17 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 1.06 million lots from 593,483 lots.
Traders said prices for the spot contracts seemed unlikely to break out of their current narrow ranges with most investors keeping their eyes on the A share market.
